title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary + kv-batching + scheduler tweaks
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Long-sequence and KV-cache-heavy workloads showed 5-12% latency regressions and reduced throughput in the previous FlashAttention rollout when ROTary (rope) codepaths fell back to slow elementwise ops. This PR upgrades the attention kernel selection and implements fused ops and rotary/rope-friendly kernels, plus scheduler improvements for continuous batching and KV caching to improve steady-state throughput and tail latency.  Summary of changes: 1) Add FlashAttentionV2-based kernels with explicit rope/rotary support; introduce fused QKV projection path that avoids extra memory writes for supported dtypes; 2) Add small-head optimized kernel and a head-count heuristic to select fused vs fallback path; 3) Implement a fast fallback for mismatched rotary frequency tensors to avoid slow elementwise corrections; 4) Scheduler tweaks to prioritize KV-cache warm requests for continuous batching and reduce head-of-line blocking for long context sequences; 5) KV-batching merge: combine small KV cache updates into multi-request batched updates when safe; 6) Tests: microbenchmarks, correctness test vectors (rope edge cases), and integration benchmarks for common Redwood workloads.  Behavioral notes: No API changes. Kernel selection happens at runtime based on model metadata (num_heads, head_dim, rotary embeddings flag) and runtime profiling. We avoid using fused kernels for small batches/short sequences to keep latency low at tail. All changes are behind a runtime feature flag (attn_kernel_selector=v2) controlled by config and can be rolled back per-model.  Benchmarks: See benchmarks_summary field for representative results.  Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests added. Canary rollout plan: enable attn_kernel_selector=v2 on 5% of dedicated capacity for 48 hours, compare token-cost and latency SLOs, then ramp to 100% if stable. Linear tickets linked.  Notes: This work builds on previous FlashAttention upgrades (see ENG-4020 series) and addresses regressions reported in SUP-234. The PR includes a short follow-up for docs to add new kernel-selection metrics to the console dashboards.

benchmarks_summary: Long-context T4 (seq=8192): throughput +18% (tokens/s) and p95 latency -9% compared to v1 baseline
KV-cache-heavy mix (bursting small requests): throughput +12% with 7% token-cost reduction due to KV-batching
Small-head models (heads<=8): small-head kernel improved throughput by 10% vs fallback; no regressions observed for batch_size=1 after guard
Edge-case rope frequencies: correctness tests show identical outputs to v1 within numerical tolerance (fp16)
